implementation_notes: TypeORM's QueryBuilder supports pessimistic locking through setLock('pessimistic_read'|'pessimistic_write'|...) and setOnLocked('nowait'|'skip_locked'), with an optional table list to restrict which joined tables get locked; it must run inside a transaction. Other TypeScript stacks differ: Prisma exposes no SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and expects interactive transactions with a raised isolation level instead. Whichever ORM is used, the transaction-scoped lock is only the primitive - the offline lease is the lock record with owner and timeout, i.e. the classic lock-manager structure.
pitfalls: setLock outside a transaction (or before the DataSource is initialised) protects nothing; TypeORM only guarantees the lock inside the transaction.
Locking with joins locks every joined table unless the table list is passed, as in setLock('pessimistic_write', undefined, ['post']).
Driver differences leak through the type: MySQL older than 8 accepts only pessimistic_write, so a repository that assumes PostgreSQL's for_no_key_update/for_key_share will break on another database.
